was required to be positioned in Delh i for scheduled operations on the 
morning of 17th June, 2000. The cash cost of operation of this flight 
from Calcutta to Delhi works out to Rs. 5.50 lakhs. As a general 
principle, Indian Airlines does not resort to cancellation of flights on 
account of loads, in order to maintain schedule integrity. However, on 
rare occasions, Indian Airlines has adopted a judicious approach with 
regard to combining/cancellation of flights due to poor loads. Efforts 
are made to the maximum extent pos sible to avoid inconvenience to 
passengers due to cancellation/ combining of scheduled services by 
either rerouting, providing alternate flights or hotel accommodation 
and subsequently providing seats on the next possible flights to their

953. SHRI SATISH PRAD HAN: Will the Minister of 
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:

load cargo;

THE MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD 
YADAV): (a) There are no such inst ances where cargo has been off-

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) Sir, the criteria 
for keeping a telephone in safe custody in MTNL is based on 
subscriber's request; depending upon the period of safe custody—(i) 
for safe custody period upto six months, full rental is being charged and 
telephone number as well as cable pair are kept reserved (ii) for safe 
custody period beyond six months 40% of the rental is being charged and 
telephone number and cable pair are not kept reserved. 
However, full rental will be charged for the entire period of safe 
custody if the telephone number and the cable pair are required to be kept 
reserved. 
 In case of a telephone under safe custody for a period beyond 
six months, where there is no specific request by the party to keep the 
telephone number & cable pair reserved on full rentals; the telephone 
number can be allotted to other party. 
 Yes, Sir.

11.10.1999 on subscriber's request for AH India shift to Rajkot 
[Gujarat].

the issuance of "Surrender Certificate" by MTNL, the party

984.  PROF.  M.  SANKARALINGAM:  Will the  Minister of

deal with the cross border smuggling on Indian borders, especially on 
Indo-Nepal and Indo-Pak border; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI V. DHANANJAY KUMAR): (a) and (b) In order to check 
cross border smuggling and other anti-India activities on Indo-Pak 
border, fencing/flood lighting works in Punjab and Rajasthan sectors 
has been completed. Further, G overnment has recently approved a 
comprehensive proposal for construction of fencing/flood lighting on

under customs having jurisdiction ove r Indo-Pak border are also on 
high alert and vigilant to detect and prevent cross border smuggling of 
contraband goods. 
As for Indo-Nepal border, to check cross border smuggling and 
other anti-India activities, States bordering Nepal have been advised 
to strengthen policing/patrolling and maintain strict vigil on the 
border. Customs formations and PRI officers are also keeping strict 
watch on the movement of third country goods to Nepal on import 
from Calcutta port, to prevent deflection/diversion into India,

 if so, the action taken in this regard alongwith the guidelines 
issued to the banks by Government; and 
 if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL): (a) to (e) No, Sir. Reserve 
Bank of India (RBI) has issued the following guidelines to commercial 
banks regarding the procedure for charging/ compounding interest on 
loan accounts: 
(i) In respect of direct agricultural advances, banks should not 
compound interest in case of current dues, i.e. crop loans and 
instalments not fallen due in respect of term loans, as the

the   principal   amount   in   respect   of  short-term 
advances to small and marginal farmers. 
RBI has also advised Commercial Banks that in the case of long 
duration crops like sugarcane etc. banks should charge interest at 
annual rates and compound the interest only if the loan/lnstalment 
becomes overdue.

 whether Government are aware of the observations of CRI 
SIL that the asset quality continues to  be the main handicap of Indian 
Banking system; 
 if so, what are the other observations made by CRISIL; and 
 what are Government's comments on the observations? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL): (a) In an analysis of the key 
risk factors impacting rating of  Indian Banks, the Credit Rating 
Information Services of India Limite d (CRISIL) have observed that it 
considers asset quality to be the main handicap of the Indian Banking 
system. 
 The same analysis while noting that Indian Banks still have a 
long way to go in upgrading credit risk management systems also 
takes note of the strengths of the sector such as a strong liquidity 
profile, limited vulnerability to external capital flows and the 
likelihood of support to public sector  banks arising from Government 
ownership. 
 Government as the owner or the majority shareholder and RBI 
as a regulator are confident that with the provisoning requirements 
being continuously tightened and ot her prudential norms being made 
more rigorous, as well as the increased awareness of the importance of 
an improved asset quality by the bank management's, the health of the 
Indian banking system is fundament ally sound. One significant aspect 
which should be noted is that in th e classification of assets the extent 
of provision is not netted out as is being done in other countries and 
hence figures of gross NPAs, whic h is often taken adverse note of, 
includes a significant component for which provisions are held by the 
banks.

1028. SHRI V, P. DURAISAMY: Will the Minister of FINANCE 
be pleased to state: 
 whether India Development Forum which met in Paris for the 
first time after the Pokhran nuclear test in May 1998, did not pledge 
any fresh aid by donor countries led by the World Bank; 
 whether it is a fact that there was no fresh commitment 
indicating that the economic sanctions  imposed after the nuclear tests 
have not been fully lifted; and 
 what steps his Ministry will take to get assistance from them 
for poverty alleviation programmes and for effecting fiscal 
consolidation in the medium term both at the Centre and State? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI YASHWANT SINHA); 
(a) Issues relating to sanctions and fresh commitments were not 
discussed at the India Development Forum Meeting held in May, 
2000. The agenda of the meeting fo cused on issues relating to 
effectiveness and relevance of external assistance in the framework of 
development planning in India and the need for structuring external 
aid to be consistent with the economic priorities of the country. The 
theme for discussion this year at the IDF was "Poverty-States 5 
Dimension". 
 No, Sir. Most of the major donors continue to make fresh 
commitments. The actual commitments made during 1999-2000 were 
USS 2093.66 million. 
 Most of the Donors/External agencies did not impose 
sanctions on programmes projects relating to Basic Human Needs, 
Hence, we continue to receive external assistance for poverty 
alleviation programmes. As per the 9th Plan document the total Met 
external assistance provides only 7% of the total plan investment. 
Fiscal consolidation is an ongoing process in the Ministry of Finance. 
For containing fiscal deficit, a number of measures have been initiated 
by the Ministry of Finance which include; setting up of a committee 
for examining the possibility of a strong institutional mechanism 
embodied in a Fiscal Responsibility Act, constitution of

1031. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Will the Minister of LAW, 
JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 whether pendency of all types of cases including those 
relating to litigation between two or more corporates is a cause of 
concern both for Government and the judiciary; 
 if so, whether any steps have been taken for the speedy 
disposal of such cases; and 
 if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF 
INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING AND MINISTER OF 
STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY 
AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY): (a) to (c) Pendency of all types of 
cases including those relating to corporate litigation between two or more 
corporates, is a cause of concern for both the Government and the 
Judiciary. Various steps have been taken by the Government for the 
speedy disposal of all cases. These include amendment in the Code of 
Civil Procedure and the Code of Criminal Procedure, increase in the

modes of dispute resolution, such as, arbitration and conciliation. Lok 
Adalats have been given a statutory base as supplementary forums for 
resolution of disputes.

to expedite disposal of cases include, inter alia, more practical 
categorisation and grouping of cases, non-accumulation of defective 
matters, setting up of specialised benches etc.

Hijacking of Italian merchant vessel 
1048. SHRI KRISHNA KUMAR BIRL A: Will the Minister of 
SURFACE TRANSPORT be pleased to state: 
 whether an Italian merchant vessel was recently hijacked on 
its way to Kandla Port in Gujarat; 
 if so, what are the details thereof; and 
 what action has been taken by Government to rescue the 
vessel from the hijackers? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
SURFACE TRANSPORT (SHRI HUKUMDEO NARAYAN 
YADAV): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) The Coast Guard Regional Headquarters, Mumbai 
received information from Chairman , Kandla Port Trust on 9th June, 
2000 that Merchant Vessel Medstar registered at Kings Town has 
reportedly been hijacked by 14 stowaways who had boarded the 
vessel at Port Bandar Abbas, Iran. The stowaways comprising 10 
Iranians and 04 Iraqis claimed to have bomb with them and 
threatened to blow the ship if th eir instructions were not followed. 
The ship after loading 312 MT of granite at Bandar Abbas was 
scheduled to arrive at Kandla Port on 11th June 2000. 
On 10th June, 2000 at about 2330 hrs the Master of the Ship 
reported that the vessel was 270 NM West of Okha and slowly 
heading towards East. The vessel wa s subsequently located by Coast 
Guard Ships at about 0230 hrs on 12th June approximately 70 NM 
due West of Okha well within the Indian EEZ. Thereafter, the vessel 
was kept under constant surveillance by the two CG Ships. The vessel 
remained adrift at the same position till a bout 1600 hrs on 12th June 
and escorted by CG Ships to Mumbai as per the request of the owners 
and the negotiators of the P&I Club in Germany, The vessel under CG 
escort arrived outer anchorage off Mumbai about 1930 hrs on 13th 
June, 2000 and remained under CG surveillance. The vessel was 
thereafter shifted to inner anchorage at about 1345 hrs on 14th June to 
facilitate boarding of the vessel by  investigating agencies. At about 
1620 hrs a bomb disposal squad of Mumbai Police and Joint 
Investigation   Team   (JIT)   comprising   representatives   of   Navy, 
189 

RAJYA SABHA [1 August, 2000] 
Customs, CBI and IB boarded the vessel and carried out the 
investigation onboard ship. The Commander, Coast Guard 
Region(West) provided assistance to the immigration authorities to 
carryout independent interrogati on. Representative from P&I Club, 
Bremen, Germany who arrived at Mu mbai alongwith an interpreter, 
also negotiated with the stowaways from 14—20 June, 2000. 
Consequently, the 10 Iranian stowaways were issued with travel 
documents by Iranian Embassy to travel by air and they left on 23rd 
June, 2000. The vessel sailed from Mumbai on 24th June with 04 Iraqi 
stowaways under escort of private security agencies hired by the 
owners of the vessel for Bandar Abbas via Kandla.

Punjab, Haryana, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan are facing a steady fall in 
their ground water levels and the exploitation level in these four States

Haryana, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan is 93.85%, 83.88%, 60.44% and

(c) Water being a State subject , steps to augment ground water 
resources is to be taken by the concerned State Government. The 
steps taken by the Union Government to increase ground water level 
in the country include:—  
(i) Constitution of Central Gr ound Water Authority under the 
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 for regulation and 
control of ground water management and development. 
(ii) Circulation of a Model Bill to all the States/Union Territories, 
to enable them to enact suitable legislation for regulation and 
control of ground water development. 
(iii) Circulation of Manual on artif icial recharge of ground water 
to the States/Union Territories to  enable them to formulate 
area specific artificial recharge schemes to check the declining 
trend in ground water levels.

artificial recharge of ground water in some 'Over-exploited' 
and 'Dark' blocks of the country.

been using lEDs. They have also come to notice stockpiling explosives for use 
during elections.

forces of the three States have revealed that a group known as Deendar
